The greatest number that divides 290 and 460 leaving remainders 4 and 5 respectively is
questions.explanation: The number must divide 290 − 4 = 286 and 460 − 5 = 455. 286 = 2 × 11 × 13 and 455 = 5 × 7 × 13, so the HCF is 13.

questions.question: The least number which leaves remainder 4 when divided by 6, 9, 15 and 18 and is exactly divisible by 7 is
questions.explanation: LCM(6, 9, 15, 18) = 90, so numbers of the form 90k + 4 are candidates. 90k + 4 must be divisible by 7: k = 4 gives 364 = 7 × 52.

questions.question: The greatest number that divides 1305, 4665 and 6905 leaving the same remainder in each case is
questions.explanation: The required number is the HCF of the differences: 4665 − 1305 = 3360 and 6905 − 4665 = 2240. HCF(3360, 2240) = 1120.

The largest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 12, 15, 18 and 27 is
questions.explanation: LCM = 2² × 3³ × 5 = 540. 9999 ÷ 540 = 18.5, so the largest multiple is 540 × 18 = 9720.

questions.question: The product of two numbers is 4107 and their HCF is 37. The greater number is
questions.explanation: The numbers are 37a and 37b with a, b co-prime and 37² × ab = 4107, so ab = 3. Hence a = 1, b = 3 and the numbers are 37 and 111.

questions.question: The LCM of 1/2, 2/3 and 3/4 is
questions.explanation: LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators = LCM(1, 2, 3) ÷ HCF(2, 3, 4) = 6 ÷ 1 = 6.
